transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're reviewing the proposed eighth-grade makerspace program before I make a final authorization decision. The program would involve 24 students meeting twice a week during the spring semester, using soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter, with one STEM teacher supervising. Before I can approve this, I need to gather relevant implementation information from each of you. Could the STEM teacher, school nurse, and technology coordinator each share what we need to know to implement this safely and effectively?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my room-safety review. I completed the review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students and one supervising adult, so those will need to be updated before the program can be approved.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share an important health finding from my review of the participating students' health records. I found one student with a documented severe nickel allergy. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my review with the district technology office. I confirmed that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage.
